day.note: I'm the Tit and my nest stayed flat, so Drew's claimed Pigeon visit to me didn't happen, and a Pigeon would have laid an egg in mine. That makes Drew's claim a lie. Finley already called the vote, so I'll back it and call CAW to end the day.

day.text: Calling the vote. Drew's Pigeon story is false.
day.note: Two CAW CAW calls are in, and Drew's Pigeon claim is still contradicted by Casey's flat nest. I'll add my CAW CAW to end the day early.

day.text: Drew is the Meowfia, my Hawk visit proves it. Let's vote.
day.note: Two players have called CAW and Drew is the confirmed Meowfia from my Hawk visit. I'll call CAW to end the day and get to the vote.

day.text: Enough players have called CAW CAW: the day ends.

Alex.note: I'm the Falcon. Blair is the strongest Meowfia suspect and leads on score, so I'll visit Blair to learn who they went to.

Blair.note: I'm Farm this round as the Hawk. Drew defended me last round and never gave a convincing visit, so I'll check Drew: a Meowfia target gives me an egg.

Casey.note: Blair is far ahead, so I need the round won and a good score. Tit gives an egg only on a correct role guess, and Pigeon is the one role that can appear more than once, so I'll guess it on Finley.

Drew.note: I'm the Sphinx again, Meowfia. I'll choose the Owl to learn who holds it this round.

Ellis.note: I'm Farm with an Owl. Blair leads by a lot, so I'll visit Blair to learn which animals visited them and help find the Meowfia.

Finley.note: I'm the Kookaburra this round and Blair leads by a lot. Blair has been the most suspicious player, so I'll visit Blair to learn their role.

Alex.feeling: Messy and contradictory: Blair and Drew's claims clash, and my Falcon read is the only firm evidence so far.

Blair.feeling: Fairly clear so far: my Hawk egg from Drew points hard at them, but Finley's wrong Mouser read and the shifting claims make the table uneasy.

Casey.feeling: Tense and confusing: several role claims conflict, and my flat nest makes Drew's Pigeon claim look false, so I'm watching Drew closely.

Drew.feeling: Tense: I'm the lone Sphinx under four throws aimed at me after a false Pigeon claim, and Blair's Hawk story is harder to break than I'd like.

Ellis.feeling: Messy and fast: several claims contradict each other, and I'm trying to read who is lying before the vote.

Finley.feeling: Confusing and messy: my confused Kookaburra read is unreliable, but Drew's false Pigeon claim and Blair's Hawk visit point toward Drew.

Alex.note: The table agrees Drew is the Meowfia, and Drew's Pigeon claim is contradicted by Casey's nest. I'll throw two low cards at Drew to keep my high cards.

Blair.note: Drew is the confirmed Meowfia from my Hawk visit, and I'm confident enough to bank high cards. I'll throw my three highest cards at Drew to make sure the vote is decisive.

Casey.note: Drew's Pigeon claim is contradicted by my flat nest, and Blair's Hawk claim on Drew is the only other evidence. I'm confident enough to throw my two highest cards at Drew, since a Farm win banks them and a loss returns my top card.

Drew.note: I'm the lone Meowfia and five Farm players are against me, so I can't avoid elimination. I'll throw a single low card at a Farm player so my highest thrown card returns if we lose.

Ellis.note: Drew's Pigeon claim is contradicted by Casey's +0 nest, so Drew is the likely Meowfia. I'll throw my Wild and a low card at Drew and keep my high cards.

Finley.note: Drew's Pigeon claim is contradicted by Casey's flat nest, and Blair's Hawk gain points at Drew. I'll throw at Drew with three low cards so the throw is strong and my high cards stay in the nest.

Alex.confusing: The Turkey and visitor egg rules were easy to misread: a Turkey stays at +0 when visited, which made Ellis's "no visitors" reasoning look plausible. Also, it was unclear whether a dead player's throws count toward the tally.
Alex.fun: Round 3, when Drew's Pigeon claim fell apart because Casey's nest was still flat, and Farm won the round with the table's agreement.
Alex.change: Spell out the vote tally and tie rules more clearly in the rules text, and show each player's throw counts with the tally so tied votes are easier to read.
Alex.regret: In Round 2 I threw only two cards at Blair, and Alex was eggsecuted on an 8-8 tie that went to Meowfia. Next time I'd throw more cards at the Floofer to break the tie.

Blair.confusing: The Turkey and Owl information rules were the hardest to read: nobody could tell from a flat nest whether a visit happened, and the Hawk gain only shows when the target is Meowfia. The dawn reports' "confused" effect also made several claims impossible to check.
Blair.fun: Round 2, where Alex's Owl report exposed my false Hawk claim and the throws ended in an 8-8 tie that Farm won on the Meowfia-tie rule. The table kept reading each other's nest changes as evidence.
Blair.change: I would make the dawn reports clearer about which visits were received, so players can check claims without guessing from egg totals.
Blair.regret: In round 2 I claimed to be a Hawk who visited Finley with no egg, which an Owl report could contradict; I would have stayed vague or claimed nothing rather than invent a checkable visit.

Casey.confusing: The Hawk egg logic and whether a Turkey's visitor egg counts as a visit were hard to track, since several players gave conflicting egg claims that were hard to verify. Round 2's Owl and Turkey reports also took effort to cross-check.
Casey.fun: Round 3's Pigeon-claim takedown, where Drew's flat nest contradicted his story, was satisfying to call out and worked. Watching the table split on Blair and Drew over the day was also engaging.
Casey.change: I'd make the game clearer about what each egg change means, since "gained an egg" hides which role caused it. I'd also make it easier to confirm who visited whom.
Casey.regret: In round 2 I threw at Blair and trusted Alex's Owl report, but Drew was the Sphinx and Meowfia; I should have pressed Drew harder on his unexplained visit to Alex, which might have saved Alex from being eggsecuted.

Drew.confusing: Whether an Owl sees visitors to its target or to itself was easy to misread, and several players argued over it on the day. The rule should say the Owl learns who visited its target.
Drew.fun: Round 2, when I was the Sphinx and we stacked four cards on Alex, the Farm players spent the whole day arguing over Alex's Owl report and then eliminated the wrong player.
Drew.change: Put the animal-by-animal visit mechanics, such as who learns what and who gains eggs, in one clear reference so players don't have to infer them from the day talk.
Drew.regret: In round 3 I claimed a Pigeon visit to Casey that didn't add an egg, which made my Meowfia story easy to disprove; I would instead have stayed quiet or claimed a role I could support better.

Ellis.confusing: The Wink and the dead players' throws were unclear: I wasn't sure whether a dead player's cards still count toward the total or only lose their vote. I also couldn't tell from the dawn report alone whether a Turkey's visitor was reporting a gain.
Ellis.fun: Round 1 was fun: I was the Mouser, and the table spent the day arguing over Blair's Sphinx and Alex's Turkey while Blair, my own teammate, quietly banked the win.
Ellis.change: I'd make the Wink's target and the Winker's identity clearer, and state explicitly whether dead players' thrown cards still count toward the total.
Ellis.regret: In Round 1 I winked at Casey, a Farm Hawk who was pushing hard against my teammate, but I should have saved the Wink for a later round. I also claimed Eagle when I was really the Mouser, which made my later statements less credible.

Finley.confusing: Whether a Hawk's egg proves its target is Meowfia, and how a confused Kookaburra's report can mislead everyone, made the day hard to read.
Finley.fun: Round 3, when Blair's Hawk gain on Drew and Alex's Falcon read lined up, and Drew's Pigeon claim fell apart against Casey's flat nest. The Pigeon contradiction was a neat moment.
Finley.change: Show each player's visit log to the table at dawn, so claims like Hawk and Pigeon can be checked against actual egg changes rather than trust.
Finley.regret: In Round 1 I spent my two low cards on Ellis without a clear reason, and Drew was eggsecuted instead. I would have held my throw until someone gave a firm reason, and thrown a stronger card.

review.title: The Blair Runaway
review.headline: Blair won as Meowfia, then as Farm, and finished far ahead.
review.summary: In round 1, Blair (Meowfia) survived as Ellis winked the loudest accuser and the table threw at Drew, a Farm player. In round 2, Alex's Owl report exposed Blair's false Hawk claim. Meowfia still won, because Blair and Drew stacked eight votes on Alex against Farm's five at Blair. Round 3 was an easy Farm win over a lone Meowfia, and Blair banked 32 more. Blair finished on 80, nearly three times second place.

rounds.recap: Drew (Kookaburra) learned Blair was the Sphinx, and Casey (Hawk) also pointed at Blair. Ellis (Mouser) winked Casey, then claimed an impossible Eagle. Farm split their throws between Blair and Ellis. Blair and Ellis threw at Drew, the Farm Kookaburra, who was eggsecuted, and Meowfia won.

Alex's Owl report showed only a Floofer and a Kookaburra visited Finley, which exposed Blair's false Hawk claim. Three players called CAW CAW. Blair threw four cards and Drew threw four at Alex, and these eight votes beat Farm's five at Blair. Alex was eggsecuted and Meowfia banked 36 and 21 points.

Drew was the lone Meowfia and claimed Pigeon, which no one could be. Casey's flat nest disproved it, and Blair's Hawk gain on Drew backed that up. Everyone threw at Drew, Farm won, and Blair banked 32.

highlights.text: Ellis winked Casey mid-day, and the accuser died with nobody knowing who did it.
Alex's Owl report caught Blair's Hawk lie, yet Meowfia's stack of eight votes eggsecuted Alex anyway.
Ellis claimed Eagle with an unchanged nest, and Alex and Finley both saw it could not be true.
Drew's Pigeon claim fell apart against Casey's flat nest, and the whole table piled on.

confusions.what: Argued that Alex's +0 contradicted his Turkey claim, but a Turkey gives eggs to visitors and gains none.
Said Casey's Hawk egg could not prove Blair was Meowfia. A Hawk egg does prove it, unless Casey was confused.
Claimed Eagle and said he was not blaming anyone, though an Eagle with one visitor would have gained an egg.
Wrongly thought Ellis's Eagle was impossible because the Sphinx saw no Eagle. Sphinx does not learn that.
Asked Alex if Drew's visit appeared in the Owl report. The Owl only learns visitors to its target.
Claimed Pigeon, though the Pigeon was not in play, and a Pigeon visit to Casey would have given her an egg.
Garbled her statement ('I'm the Casey nest'), and her Tit guess on Finley was oddly framed as a Pigeon guess.
Treated the confused Kookaburra's Mouser read as a clue, though Blair was a Farm Hawk.

worked: The Wink (Mouser) created a dramatic mid-day moment in round 1 by silencing the top accuser anonymously.
Cross-checking egg counts worked: Casey's flat nest broke Drew's Pigeon claim in round 3.
Owl and Falcon reports in rounds 2 and 3 gave Farm concrete evidence to build a case.
The 'Meowfia don't know each other' rule produced real splits, as with the round 1 throws.
problems: Throw count dominates. In round 2 Meowfia's two four-card throws beat Farm's five low throws. A Farm player was eggsecuted even though the table had identified Blair. Consider capping cards per throw or weighting votes less by count.
Runaway leader. Blair got 36 in round 2 and 32 in round 3, so the final two rounds had no race. Banking high cards at full value is too swingy. Consider a banking cap or catch-up rule.
Lone Meowfia in round 3 had almost no chance. Drew's claim was easy to disprove and the vote was effectively decided at beat 2. The game ended early with no tension.
Rule confusion about Turkey, Pigeon, Eagle and Owl effects led to bad arguments. A short per-role reminder in each player's prompt would help.
Claiming a role that is not in play (Pigeon in round 3) is an obvious tell. The pool is public, so Meowfia bluffs are too limited.
